topic: Template Class with Default Template Parameters
explanation: In C++, template classes allow the creation of generic classes that can operate with any data type. By providing default template parameters, developers can simplify class instantiation when common types are used, reducing verbosity and increasing code flexibility. This feature is essential for designing reusable, type-safe components in modern C++ programming.
code_example: std::cout << "Template class with default parameter" << std::endl;
example_explanation: This example defines a template class 'BasicStreamBuffer' with a default template parameter 'Traits' set to 'std::char_traits<T>'. In 'main', the class is instantiated with only the 'char' type, relying on the default for 'Traits'. The 'display' method demonstrates that the class is correctly instantiated and functional, illustrating how default template parameters simplify class usage in modern C++.
